target_customer: Patent law firms and in-house IP teams, about 700 teams per the company
problem: Drafting patent applications and responding to office actions is slow and done in Microsoft Word with little software support. Solve uses AI to speed drafting, prosecution and later litigation analysis.
product_category: Legal tech / AI patent drafting and prosecution

founders.name: Chris Parsonson
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch also links Dyson and Huawei experience of patent filing to the origin of the idea.

founders.name: Angus Parsonson
education: University of Bristol, MEng computer science
founders.background_notes: YC page: quantitative developer at Coremont, a Brevan Howard spin-off; GCHQ cyber security scholarship.

competitors.name: PatSnap
competitors.what: Patent search and IP analytics for R&D teams

competitors.name: Harvey AI
competitors.what: General legal AI for contracts and research, not patents

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed LLM drafting that respects patent claim structure and law with attorney review, plus security for confidential filings. Hard in part but standard product engineering around foundation models.

defensibility.rationale: Law firm workflow embedding, security certifications and accumulated attorney feedback help, but rivals like DeepIP and Patlytics address the same drafting wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent search vendors did not focus on drafting in 2023. Thomson Reuters and Microsoft became investors in 2025 rather than competitors per the sources.

market_need_then: Patent attorneys lacked software beyond Word for drafting, and TechCrunch in November 2023 reported over 25 IP firms already using it with claimed 60 to 90 percent efficiency gains and roughly 100 thousand to 1 million dollars in recurring revenue.

branding.domain_note: Uses solveintelligence.com; no purchase history found.

identity.logo: Dark and light outline wordmark per Brandfetch listing
identity.visual_style: Clean professional enterprise legal tech site with customer logos and compliance badges
identity.voice_and_tone: Efficiency and trust for attorneys, tagline 'AI for patents'

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence of community or merch found; reputation driven by named law firm customers and investor backing.

brand_strength.rationale: Credible among IP lawyers through named customers and press, but the name is descriptive and no brand story or community was found.

pivots.to: Broader patent platform adding litigation and claim charting
pivots.why: Expansion announced with the Series B and later acquisitions of Palito.ai and ClaimWise in 2026

outcome_analysis: Solve launched in July 2023 into a profession with weak software, signed 25 firms within months, and raised a 3 million seed, a 12 million Series A in April 2025 and a 40 million Series B in December 2025 for 55 million total. The company reports eight figure recurring revenue growing tenfold, then expanded by acquiring Palito.ai and ClaimWise in 2026.
notes: Seed 3M is from TechCrunch November 2023 and no exact date is given, so only the year is recorded. Angus Parsonson title CTO from TechCrunch; YC page lists him as Founder. Total 55M after Series B per IPWatchdog headline. ARR growth claim is company stated. Name origin not found.
